title: Your Voice, Your Vote
description: A new policy is being discussed in your town. Explore how citizens can participate responsibly.

begin.text: Your local council is proposing a new policy that affects your neighborhood. What is a constructive first step?

choices.text: Read the official proposal and any published meeting notes.
choices.feedback: Great start. Understanding a proposal helps you participate meaningfully.

choices.text: Share an unverified rumor about the proposal online.
choices.feedback: Spreading unverified information can mislead others and weaken public debate.

public_meeting.text: A public consultation meeting is scheduled. How do you participate?

choices.text: Attend and share your feedback respectfully during the comment period.
choices.feedback: Excellent. Respectful, informed participation strengthens democratic processes.

choices.text: Disrupt the meeting to prevent others from speaking.
choices.feedback: Disrupting a meeting can silence other citizens' right to be heard.

voting.text: The policy is later put to a local vote. What should you do?

choices.text: Vote after considering the information you have gathered.
choices.feedback: Voting is one of the most direct ways citizens shape their community.

choices.text: Skip voting entirely without any particular reason.
choices.feedback: Voting is a right -- using it, when you are able to, helps your voice count.

bad_choice.text: This path could undermine fair, informed civic participation. Let's try again.

choices.feedback: Constructive participation benefits the whole community.

finish.text: Scenario complete. Citizen rights work best when paired with informed, respectful participation in public life.
